review.assessment: The change adds a new solution.sh script using `head` and `tail` to extract line ranges from stdin. The implementation incorrectly calculates the number of lines for `tail` as `$((end - start))`, which is one less than the inclusive count required, causing the output window to shift forward by one index.

findings.defect: The pipeline calculates the tail length as $((end - start)) instead of the inclusive count ($((end - start + 1))). This results in extracting one fewer line than requested and starting from START+1 rather than START.
When START equals END, the length calculation yields zero (end - start == 0). The command effectively executes `tail -n 0`, which produces no output even though a single line should be returned.

When the requested END exceeds input length, `tail -n K` prints all available lines if asked for more than exist. This causes it to ignore the START index and print preceding lines (line 1) that should have been filtered out.
